neighbours.label: The field or institution noun in a named discipline whose modifier is a group of people ('child psychology', 'Human Relations', 'Women's Studies', 'Hunter College'), vs the same nouns after a non-person modifier and the person word before a non-field noun
fire: He wrote his thesis on the history of women's studies in Canada.
Her sister works as a counsellor trained in child psychology.
The library holds every issue of the journal Human Development since 1960.
She runs a seminar on adolescent psychology for new teachers.
The conference on child development drew researchers from twenty countries.
He teaches a course in gender studies at the local university.
The report was published by the Institute of Human Relations in London.
Her mother taught English at Barnard College for thirty years.
quiet: He wrote his thesis on the history of railway engineering in Canada.
Her sister works as a counsellor trained in cognitive psychology.
The library holds every issue of the local newspaper since 1960.
She bought a car seat for the child before the long drive.
The conference on soil chemistry drew researchers from twenty countries.
He teaches a course in organic chemistry at the local university.
The report was published by the Department of Transport in London.
Her mother taught English at the village school for thirty years.

predictions: Person-group discipline nouns 0.5-0.85; 'developmental psychology', bare 'Psychology', and 'child' + ordinary noun under 0.05.
short: field noun after a person-group modifier
notes: Card: ' psychology' x8 after 'child', ' College' x4 (Hunter College), ' Relations' (Human Relations), ' Studies' (Women's Studies), 'child study', 'Child Rights', 'kid club'. Probe: 'child psychology' 0.617, 'Human Relations' 0.856, 'Hunter College' 0.799; 'developmental psychology' 0.011, bare 'Psychology' 0.031, 'toy for the child' 0.008. So the modifier matters, not the field word.
